query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these incident tickets.

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents from short_description into device/service types (printer, monitor, database, network) gives a strong grouping axis for analysis. Sample values are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: failure_type
per_column.rationale: A distinct failure-mode axis useful for pattern analysis. Mostly well-grounded, but some inference is loose: 'Printer not working properly' mapped to 'not_responding_unresponsive' while a nearly identical 'not functioning' printer became 'service_failure', showing inconsistent/under-supported distinctions from terse text.

per_column.name: resolution_action_type
per_column.rationale: A resolution-oriented axis is analytically valuable. However the source rows are short_description only with no resolution notes; asserting 'repair_needed' or 'connectivity_fix' as an action outcome is largely inferred from category rather than grounded in stated resolution text, so specificity outruns evidence.

per_column.name: self_resolved
per_column.rationale: Potentially useful if grounded, but nothing in the sampled source text indicates whether an incident self-resolved; opened/closed timestamps are identical placeholders. Values like True/False appear asserted without textual support, indicating invented specificity.

per_column.name: is_repeat_incident_type
per_column.rationale: Heavily skewed (452 true) and the flag cannot be derived from a single row's short_description; determining a repeat requires cross-row comparison not evidenced here. Confident True/False values are largely unsupported by the row-level source text.

per_column.name: urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: An urgency axis could aid prioritization analysis and partly overlaps existing 'priority'. Some values are reasonable ('Internet connectivity lost'->immediate_attention), but many terse descriptions offer no explicit urgency cue, so 'standard'/'immediate_attention' are partly inferred beyond the text.

judge.rationale: The categorical columns (incident_category, failure_type, urgency_signal) provide genuinely new grouping/comparison axes well suited to exploring the tickets and are mostly grounded in short_description. The action/behavioral flags (resolution_action_type, self_resolved, is_repeat_incident_type) are analytically appealing but their confident values are largely inferred or asserted beyond what the short, resolution-free source text supports, and some show inconsistent categorization. Overall useful set with moderate groundedness concerns on the inferred behavioral columns.
